law: src/laws/browserWalk.test.ts:567-574 ("live metadata takes the quiet token, not the dim one"). The LIVE list requires the exact `.focus-skip` rule to contain `color: var(--tx-quiet)`.
why: "Not This One" (FocusScreen.tsx:159) is a bare-words tappable control drawn in --tx-quiet. The key gives tappable non-button text --tint, and §AL says a control is never bare words. The finding's fix, --tint on .focus-skip, would fail this law. §AL offers another route: make it the quiet option, `className="quiet-action"` in FocusScreen.tsx (press-1 fill, pill, --tx-2). That also clears §AL, but it needs a file I do not own. The lead should either amend the law, dropping .focus-skip from LIVE with a dated reason, or take the quiet-action route in FocusScreen.tsx.

law: src/laws/browserWalk.test.ts:567-574 (LIVE list pins `.receipt-line` to `color: var(--tx-quiet)`), with the BROWSER-F-09 note on the rule itself
why: The finding adds `button.receipt-line { color: var(--tint) }`. That would pass the law's text match, because only the base rule is read. It would defeat the law's stated intent, though: the pin on --tx-quiet was written knowing every receipt line is a BUTTON ("13 More waiting" and so on), and the I5 comment says "It stays dim; the glyph does the work, not colour". Dave also moved "N more in Anytime" from a red link to this quiet line on 2026-09-11. Turning all of them red on Today, Life and Goals conflicts with that pin and that history. It needs the law amended with a dated reason, or the finding rejected. I did not game the law with an override. The 11px-caps half (#42) is applied.

law: src/laws/browserWalk.test.ts line ~414-424, "the sheet and toast verbs take it"
why: The finding is real: in dark, every .row-act inside a sheet (Add Item, Add a Window, Edit Routine) paints a white label. `.form-sheet .row-act` and `.sheet-scrim > .card .row-act` (components.css:1588/1590, 0,3,0) set it to --tint-on-sheet (#FFFFFF), which beats the capsule's --tint. The correct fix is to delete those two selectors. The capsule now carries an opaque --capsule-fill (#17171A), where --tint measures 4.82:1, so the white-label workaround for a translucent sheet grey no longer applies. Light is unaffected, because --accent-tx in light is #BC000E, the same as --on-light-red. The law loops over [".sheet-bar-save", ".row-act", ".note-fix", ".toast-action"] and requires each in the --tint-on-sheet selector list, so the law must drop ".row-act". I did not work around it with a later override, because that would defeat the law's stated intent.

It requires ".fact.purp" to be in components.css, so the correct fix (delete the purple text variant, since purple is not in the key) fails it. The same file's "every fact variant the app renders has a rule somewhere" would also fail while the six call sites still render `purp`. Amend in place once the call sites move: take ".fact.purp" out of the required list and add it to the not.toContain retired-variant check beside ".fact.sky".

law: src/laws/browserWalk.test.ts:599-607, 'the deliberately dimmed states recede to secondary, never to --tx-4'
why: The finding is real now. On a paid bill row, 'Paid Sep 1' (`.r-goal.r-cat`, `--tx-3` regular) sits beside '$1,800' (`.ruled .task-row .money-amt.paid`, `--tx-2`, which is the same hex, and semibold because the ruled base rule sets `--w-semi`). This law requires that exact selector to exist with `color: var(--tx-2)`, a 2026-09-14 ruling that §AK V5.2 and §AM have since overtaken. Amend it to drop `.ruled .task-row .money-amt.paid` from its list (or pin `--good` for it), with a dated reason. A more-specific override rule would get around the law without meeting its intent, so it was not added. Without a law change, the fallback is to mark the sub line `r-goal fact good` in MoneyFlow.tsx:611 when paid. That does not work either: `.ruled .r-goal.r-cat` (0,3,0) out-ranks `.fact.good` (0,2,0), so that markup would also need a ruled rule.
